summary: the packet case, whose packetprobe requires each bound packet socket to have a row of /proc/net/packet and none after its close, against a close that keeps its binding

argv: sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel
ARCH=i686 exec sh tests/proofs/guest.sh run packet 'run: packet: PASS'

faults.name: unbind
faults.summary: the last close of a packet socket returns before the teardown, so its binding stays on the list the receive path walks, with the socket it delivers to

lines: guest.packet.packetprobe on i686: failure: close-frees failed: a closed packet socket was still in /proc/net/packet
